title: mitstack lifecycle webhook response
description: Versioned wire-shape contract for the JSON body a block owner's registered webhook endpoint returns to mitstack's lifecycle engine for a subscribe/unsubscribe/upgrade/validate call (MIT-1136, the response half of the bidirectional contract envelope.schema.json pins on the request side). Mirrors api/internal/lifecycle.webhookResponse byte-for-byte for every property but resources, which reports the outcome of each declared resource's ensure, observe and delete calls by name. Additive-friendly: additionalProperties is true at every level so a new optional response field never breaks an existing operator or this contract test. Nothing is required: a verb with nothing to report legitimately answers {}.

credential.description: The credential a capability issued the app an issue named, present only in the answer to an issue. Its values are secret.

replaces.description: On a validate, the names of the declared resources the block's upgrade would replace rather than change in place.

outputs.description: Manifest-declared, non-secret outputs the operator produced (T-473). A Go nil map encodes to JSON null, and shipping operators emit exactly that on a verb with nothing to return, so null is tolerated alongside an object of string values.

secretOutputs.description: Secret outputs the operator produced, resolved server-side into the org secret store. Same null tolerance as outputs.

error.description: Human-readable failure message surfaced on a 4xx/5xx response.

pending.description: True when an async operator's resource is still converging (T-473 finalize) — the engine keeps polling validate instead of settling active with possibly-incomplete outputs.

statusDetail.description: Additive human-readable progress detail (T-576), e.g. what an async operator is doing while pending.

lastError.description: Additive human-readable detail of the most recent transient failure (T-576).

absent.description: The explicit teardown-verify marker (MIT-1125, AbsenceProber). A POINTER-shaped field: true/false means the operator explicitly reported whether the resource is gone; the field's absence (never present in the JSON at all) means the operator does not implement the marker and the engine fails open. Because JSON has no way to distinguish "absent from the object" from "explicitly null" once decoded into a nullable Go pointer, null is accepted here too and carries the same fail-open meaning as omitting the field.

resourceSecretOutputs.description: Each provided resource's secret outputs, keyed by the resource's name, so two resources reporting the same key each keep their own value. A resource reporting no secret output has no entry. Kept out of resources, which the engine records.

resources.description: The outcome of each call a verb ran for a resource the block's manifest declares, keyed by the resource's name. A resource the verb never reached has no entry, and within an entry a call that did not run has no key. A block served over a single resource reports none.

ensure.description: The ensure call's outcome. An empty object is an ensure that ran and succeeded.

error.description: Why the call failed, scrubbed of request secrets.

state.description: What an observe found: present, absent or unknown.

statusDetail.description: Human-readable detail the call left, scrubbed of request secrets.

identity.description: The identity the ensure stored for its resource, the values that address the resource where it lives.

type.description: A type the call reported. Only an observe reports one.

error.description: Why the call failed, scrubbed of request secrets.

state.description: What the observe found: present, absent or unknown.

statusDetail.description: Human-readable detail the observe left, scrubbed of request secrets.

identity.description: The identity the observe addressed the resource by, when it was known.

type.description: The exact type the observe observed the resource as.

delete.description: The delete call's outcome. An empty object is a delete that ran and succeeded.

error.description: Why the call failed, scrubbed of request secrets.

state.description: What an observe found: present, absent or unknown.

statusDetail.description: Human-readable detail the call left, scrubbed of request secrets.

identity.description: An identity the call reported. Only an ensure or an observe reports one.

type.description: A type the call reported. Only an observe reports one.
